proposals.before: his father Xu Yuzhi was a Composition Official—both were put to death by Emperor Gao of Qi.
proposals.after: his father Xu Yuzhi was a Composition Official—both were put to death under the Taichu reign (by Liu Shao).
proposals.reason: Authoritative Nan Qi Shu witnesses read 太初 (Liu Shao's Taichu era), not 太祖; the parents were killed in AD 453 during Liu Shao's usurpation, not by Qi Emperor Gao.

proposals.before: His father Yuzhi was a Composition Official: both were killed by Taizu.
proposals.after: His father Yuzhi was a Composition Official: both were killed in the Taichu era.
proposals.reason: Packet Chinese 太祖 is almost certainly a corruption of 太初; literal English should follow the historical Taichu reading.

proposals.before: He served as a staff officer in the households of the Minister of Works and the Grand Commandant, and as Literary Scholar to Prince Anwu of Ancheng.
proposals.after: He served as a staff officer in the households of the Minister of Works and the Grand Commandant, and as Literary Scholar to the Prince of Ancheng.
proposals.reason: Standard text has 安成王 (Prince of Ancheng), not 安武王; idiomatic should not invent the hybrid Anwu of Ancheng.

proposals.before: He served as Retainer in the households of the Minister of Works and the Grand Commandant, and as Literary Scholar to Prince Anwu.
proposals.after: He served as Retainer in the households of the Minister of Works and the Grand Commandant, and as Literary Scholar to the Prince of Ancheng.
proposals.reason: Literal follows corrupt 安武王; repair to standard 安成王 / Prince of Ancheng.

proposals.before: He went out as Administrator of Jinling, then returned to serve as Junior Master to the Heir Apparent and head the Chief Office of the Imperial Park.
proposals.after: He went out as Administrator of Jinling, then returned to serve as Junior Master to the Heir Apparent and as Changshui Colonel.
proposals.reason: 長水校尉 is the Changshui Colonel, a palace guard command, not an Imperial Park office.

proposals.before: He went out as Administrator of Jinling, returned as Junior Master to the Heir Apparent, and headed the Chief Office of the Imperial Park.
proposals.after: He went out as Administrator of Jinling, returned as Junior Master to the Heir Apparent, and served as Changshui Colonel.
proposals.reason: Same mistranslation of 長水校尉 as Imperial Park.

proposals.before: Before he could take up that post he was made General Who Pacifies the North and Chief Clerk on the campaign staff of Heir Apparent Ziliang of Wenxi, then promoted to Director of the Ministry of Personnel, Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard, and finally Chief Clerk.
proposals.after: Before he could take up that post he was made General Who Pacifies the North and Chief Clerk on the campaign staff of Duke Ziliang of Wenxi, then promoted to Director of the Ministry of Personnel, Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard, and finally Chief Clerk.
proposals.reason: 聞喜公子良 is Duke Ziliang of Wenxi, not Heir Apparent; conflating 公 with 太子.

proposals.before: Prince Jingling of Ziling was very fond of him.
proposals.after: Prince Ziliang of Jingling was very fond of him.
proposals.reason: Literal reverses and garbles 竟陵王子良 as Prince Jingling of Ziling.

proposals.before: When Prince Shi'an of Yaoguang rebelled the multitude were agitated and unsettled; when Xiaosi entered the palace calm returned within.
proposals.after: When Prince Yaoguang of Shian rebelled the multitude were agitated and unsettled; when Xiaosi entered the palace calm returned within.
proposals.reason: Literal reverses 始安王遙光 as Prince Shi'an of Yaoguang; should be Prince Yaoguang of Shian.

proposals.before: In the fourth year of Jianwu, immediately upon the new reign title he was made Minister of Works with Protocol Equal to a Grand Marshal.
proposals.after: In the fourth year of Jianwu he was, while retaining his existing titles, made Equal in Ceremony to the Three Excellencies (kaifu yitong sansi).
proposals.reason: 卽本號開府儀同三司 means granted kaifu yitong sansi on his existing titles, not a new reign title and not specifically Minister of Works.

proposals.before: He was transferred to Yellow Gate Gentleman and appointed to head the Chief Office of the Imperial Park.
proposals.after: He was transferred to Yellow Gate Gentleman and appointed Changshui Colonel.
proposals.reason: 長水校尉 is Changshui Colonel, not an Imperial Park office.

proposals.before: Prince Yuzhang Jiong smoothed matters over, saying, "This surely does not diminish Zhongrong's virtue."
proposals.after: Prince Yuzhang Yi smoothed matters over, saying, "This surely does not diminish Zhongrong's virtue."
proposals.reason: 豫章王嶷 is Xiao Yi; idiomatic wrongly renders 嶷 as Jiong.

proposals.before: The emperor was in the Leyou Park; hearing of Yuzhi's rebels he told Prince Yuzhang Jiong, "At the beginning of Emperor Ming of Song the nine provinces rebelled together—such vermin merely stir; watch how Lord Xiao will thunder at your heads."
proposals.after: The emperor was in the Leyou Park; hearing of Yuzhi's rebels he told Prince Yuzhang Yi, "At the beginning of Emperor Ming of Song the nine provinces rebelled together—such vermin merely stir; watch how Lord Xiao will thunder at your heads."
proposals.reason: 豫章王嶷 is Xiao Yi; Jiong is a mistranslation of 嶷.

proposals.before: When Prince Shi'an of Yaoguang rebelled, that night he sent three hundred men to the residence to seize Wenji by surprise, wishing to make him commander-in-chief, but Wenji had already returned to the Secretariat.
proposals.after: When Prince Yaoguang of Shian rebelled, that night he sent three hundred men to the residence to seize Wenji by surprise, wishing to make him commander-in-chief, but Wenji had already returned to the Secretariat.
proposals.reason: Literal reverses 始安王遙光 as Prince Shi'an of Yaoguang.

proposals.before: As Companion to the Prince of Nankang and a graduate of the Hua selection, Zhaolue was appointed companion; soon he also served concurrently as Left Assistant Director.
proposals.after: As Companion to the Prince of Nanjun and a graduate of the Hua selection, Zhaolue was appointed companion; soon he also served concurrently as Left Assistant Director.
proposals.reason: 南郡王 is Prince of Nanjun (Southern Commandery), not Nankang.

decisions.after: his father Xu Yuzhi was a Composition Official; both his father and grandfather were put to death during the Taichu reign.
decisions.reason: The received 太祖 is a known textual error for 太初. Xu Zhan之 and Xu Yuzhi were killed during Liu Shao's Taichu usurpation in AD 453, decades before Qi's Emperor Gao ruled.

decisions.reason: 長水校尉 is Changshui Colonel, a guard command, not an office administering an imperial park.

聞喜公 identifies Ziliang as Duke of Wenxi. It does not call him heir apparent.
竟陵王子良 is Prince Ziliang of Jingling; the existing literal wording reverses and corrupts both parts.
始安王遙光 is Prince Yaoguang of Shian. The existing literal translation reverses the personal name and principality.

卽本號 means that Xiaosi retained his existing titles, while 開府儀同三司 is the honor Equal in Ceremony to the Three Excellencies. The old translation invents both an era change and a Minister of Works appointment.
As in s0020, 長水校尉 is Changshui Colonel.
豫章王嶷 is Xiao Yi, Prince of Yuzhang. Jiong is an incorrect reading of 嶷.
This second 豫章王嶷 is likewise Xiao Yi, not Jiong.
The literal field again reverses Prince Yaoguang's personal name and principality.
南郡王 is Prince of Nanjun, not Prince of Nankang.

claimRetractions.reason: The title was inferred solely from the corrupt Taizu reading; the sentence instead refers to the Taichu era.
This hybrid title was generated from a corrupt Chinese graph and should not survive beside the corrected Prince of Ancheng claim.
Ziliang is explicitly Duke of Wenxi here; the heir-apparent title is a mistranslation.
This false combined title is based on the incorrect Jiong reading; the record already has separate correct Yi and Prince of Yuzhang claims.

Follow the collated 安成王 reading in both languages.
Correct the reading of 嶷 in Xiao Yi's given name.
Correct Jiong to Yi while preserving the combined title reference.
